tags.sinking_method: scuttled by crew (seacocks opened, fires set) per Wikipedia and Pure Diving; boiler-explosion account disputed
tags.note: Lies on port side in Malmok Bay; shallowest about 5m, deepest at propeller about 16.5-18m (Wikipedia 18m, Pure Diving 17m, JADS 16.5m). Storm damage had broken the hull amidships by 1953 (Wikipedia; Divernet also describes storm damage). Length conflict: Wikipedia 121.4m/398.3ft, Divernet 121m, Frommer's 394ft, Pure Diving 130m/400ft, JADS about 144m/430ft. Tonnage: Wikipedia lists 4,363 GRT and 2,164 NRT; Divernet gives 2,164 tons. Sinking: scuttled by crew 10 May 1940 as Dutch marines approached (Wikipedia, Pure Diving, Divernet; Wikipedia's shipwreck list gives 11 May). Cause conflict: Divernet attributes the sinking to a boiler explosion, Wikipedia states the boiler-explosion account is false.

Shallow sandy bowl (inner reef about 17.5m per JADS) plus outer reef; outer reef max 25m (Duikersgids), 30m (JADS), 33m (Aruba.com). Kappel tugboat wreck at about 12-15m (Wikipedia 12m, JADS 15m). Shore entry; outer reef can have current in wind (Duikersgids).

Sandy bay near Malmok, shore entry via steps (Aruba.com) and sandy beach (Duikersgids). Depth conflict: Duikersgids 15m; Tropical Snorkeling gives 2-5ft for the adjacent Catalina Cove snorkel area. Snorkel guides report little to see directly off the beach and more life toward Catalina Cove.

Reef max 16m (JADS, Duikersgids), 12m per Palm Beach Divers, 15m per Aruba.com. Scattered Lockheed Lodestar wreckage at about 11-12m (Duikersgids, Frommer's). Known for turtles; Duikersgids describes a turtle feeding and cleaning area. Boat dive per Duikersgids.

Only the midsection remains, about 7.6-8m depth (Wikipedia 25ft/7.6m, Pure Diving 25ft, Palm Beach Divers 8m). Fore and aft sections were joined and the ship sailed to Baltimore; scrapped 1959 (Divernet, Willemsubmerged). Midsection fate is a source conflict: Wikipedia says used as Dutch Navy bombing target, Willemsubmerged says that is unconfirmed and munitions found suggest US Army Air Force practice. Length (355ft) appears in one source only and is not used.

Cement freighter launched 1959 as Blackthorn, later Jane Sea (locally Jane C); sunk 4 September 1988 as an artificial reef. Upright; bow about 18m, propeller 27-28m (Pure Diving, Duikersgids, JADS); Divernet reports propeller at 30m. No penetration per JADS; current medium to strong per Duikersgids. Length conflict: Pure Diving/Willemsubmerged 57m (190ft), DreamWrecks 170ft, Divernet 76m. Abandonment story conflict: cocaine seizure vs engine trouble/unpaid dues and embargo (Willemsubmerged records Ports Authority archives for the latter). Tonnage (749) appears in one source only and is not used.

Hard coral reef max about 25m per JADS; Aruba.com lists max 36m with strong deep currents and rates it challenging for advanced divers; Diveplannerpro rates it Advanced. Aruba.com reports large barracuda and horse mackerel (jacks).

Duikersgids lists a 12m shore dive with 20-30m visibility and limited current. Depth conflict: Aruba.com max 21m; Guide to Caribbean Vacations describes Malmok Reef and Debbie II at about 70ft roughly 2 miles off the coast (possibly a separate boat site with the same name).

Two aircraft off Renaissance Island: an older twin-prop Convair (model conflict: Convair 240 per Pure Diving; Convair 340 per Palm Beach Divers and JADS; Convair 240 or DC-3 per Scuba.com and Atlas & Boots) scattered by storms/Hurricane Lenny 1999 (Scuba.com, Divernet), and an Air Aruba NAMC YS-11 sunk 2004 (Scuba.com, Divernet), intact with nose up. Depths: Pure Diving and Palm Beach Divers Convair 14-22m, YS-11 cockpit 16m to tail 27m; Scuba.com YS-11 about 14m to 23m and Convair moved to about 24m. Drug-seizure history of the Convair reported by Scuba.com and Divernet only (not by operator pages). Seats and doors removed from YS-11 before sinking.

Slope reaching about 100ft/33m (JADS), max 30m (Aruba.com); search-result summaries from DiveBuddy and Scuba Diving describe a drop-off to 110-130ft. Site type wall retained on the basis of drop-off descriptions; JADS and Aruba.com describe a slope/coral shelf. DiveBuddy and scubadiving.com evidence is from search-result snippets only.

Depth 25-90ft (Visit Aruba), max 27m (Aruba.com). Large gorgonian clusters, brain, flower and star corals, purple and orange sponges; barracuda reported by Visit Aruba and Frommer's. Location: near Mangel Halto per Visit Aruba; off De Palm Island per Frommer's. Level Beginner per Visit Aruba.

Coral slope off De Palm Island, 15-120ft (Visit Aruba, Guide to Caribbean Vacations); Duikersgids lists 20m. Drift diving; Intermediate per Visit Aruba. Boat dive, also reachable from shore once on Palm Island (Duikersgids). A Cessna 414 wreck lies off Palm Island (Duikersgids, Wikipedia).

tags.name: California
tags.note: SS California, British steamship wrecked 23 September 1891 (Wikipedia California Lighthouse article; ScubaBoard thread quoting Aruba Bound). Northeast coast, max depth 14m (Wikipedia, Divers Guide), strong currents. Divers Guide calls it an unidentified wreck nicknamed SS California. Divers Guide lists bull and hammerhead sharks; no other source corroborates, so no species are named in the markdown.
